name_note: GTDB's Allisonella is broader than the classical genus: besides Allisonella histaminiformans it contains Allisonella pneumosinta, whose genomes are deposited in NCBI as Dialister pneumosintes.

sentences.text: Allisonella histaminiformans is an ovoid, Gram-negative-staining bacterium isolated from the faeces of grain-fed cattle and from the caecum of a horse.
It appears to use histidine decarboxylation as its sole mechanism of energy derivation, producing histamine, with lysine the only other amino acid used.
A study reported that its growth was stimulated by yeast extract, protein hydrolysates and water-soluble extracts of alfalfa or corn silage, indicating a peptide requirement.

In a randomized placebo-controlled trial of faecal microbiota transplantation in hypertensive patients, increased abundance of Allisonella histaminiformans was reported to correlate with office systolic blood pressure.
Another study reported that Allisonella histaminiformans, with Streptococcus mutans, could serve as a potential biomarker for NAFLD-associated mild cognitive impairment.

Dialister pneumosintes, placed in this genus by GTDB, has been described as a slow-growing obligate anaerobe commonly found in the oral cavity, nasopharynx, gastrointestinal tract and vaginal microbiota.
